land.text: 'the Vikings had set up their Kingdom of Dublin from territory previously belonging to Leinster' (Leinster article)
Dublin, taken by the Normans in 1170; the last king was killed in 1171

capitals.name: Dublin
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Capital: Dublin'; the site of the longphort is 'hotly debated'.

correction.text: 'Its territory corresponded to most of present-day County Dublin'; 'in peaceful times it extended roughly as far as Wicklow' with Leixlip to the west and Skerries to the north

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Dublin. A 25 km radius round Dublin stands for most of County Dublin (about 925 km2 in all); the peaceful-times extent to Wicklow is not drawn. No area on the page.

ledger.note: 853: the Norse kingdom of Dublin. Infobox 'Established: 853'; the kingdom 'lasted from roughly 853 AD to 1170 AD'; 'It was the first and longest-lasting Norse kingdom in Ireland'; Amlaib Conung is co-king from c. 853. The page gives no 839 or 841 founding; 'The Vikings may have first over-wintered in 840-841'.

1170: the Normans take Dublin. 'Norman conquest: 1170' (infobox); Hasculf (Ascall mac Ragnaill) was 'deposed in 1170' and 'killed attempting to regain kingship in 1171'; the Norman force 'stormed the town and took it' on 21 September (Norman invasion article).

wars.name: Norman conquest of Dublin
wars.outcome: Dublin taken in September 1170; the last king killed in 1171 while trying to retake it.

wars.name: Gaelic conquest of Dublin (988)
wars.outcome: 'In 988, Mael Sechnaill mac Domnaill led the initial Gaelic conquest of Dublin'; the kings of Dublin lived on under Gaelic overlords.
wars.note: Later overlordships on the page: Leinster influence from the mid-11th century, Toirdelbach Ua Briain 'seized overlordship of Dublin following Diarmait's death' (1072), and Enna Mac Murchada 'reigned under Ui Conchobair overlordship' (1122-1126). Their end dates are not given, so no vassal events are recorded.

certainty.note: The page gives towns, not a boundary.

notes: Waterford (Norse town, taken August 1170) has no dossier. The Leinster dossier records the loss of Dublin to this state in 853 (confidence 2). Rulers table on the page: Amlaib Conung c. 853-871, Imar c. 857-873, Hasculf deposed 1170; no ruler strip because the list is not in a form read here. Dublin and York (Jorvik) were linked by their Norse rulers (lead) but with no dates.
